context.title: Judah's Borders and Towns
context.summary: Judah's borders are traced, Caleb takes Hebron and Debir, and his daughter Achsah asks him for springs of water. A long list of Judah's towns follows, ending with the note that the Jebusites still held Jerusalem.
context.background: Judah stretched from the Dead Sea ('the salt sea') to the Mediterranean, with the dry Negev to the south. The northern border ran through the valley of the son of Hinnom just below Jerusalem (v. 8), a valley later linked with child sacrifice and with the name Gehenna. The towns are grouped by region: the south, the lowland ('the valley,' v. 33), the hill country and the wilderness.

customs.note: In the dry south, land without a water source was of little use. Achsah's request secured her family's future.

watchFor: Othniel, who takes Debir (v. 17), later becomes Israel's first judge (Judges 3:9).
Achsah speaks up for herself and is answered generously (vv. 18–19).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: Reuben
people.summary: Behold a son!, the eldest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 29:32). His sinful conduct, referred to in Gen. 35:22, brought down upon him his dying father’s malediction (48:4).

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel.

people.name: Caleb
people.summary: The son of Jephunneh (Num. 13:6; 32:12; Josh. 14:6, 14). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus.

people.name: Jephunneh
people.summary: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan (Num. 13:6), a Kenezite (Josh. 14:14).

people.name: Anak
people.summary: Long-necked, the son of Arba, father of the Anakim (Josh. 15:13; 21:11, Heb. Anok).

people.name: Ahiman
people.summary: One of the three giant Anakim brothers whom Caleb and the spies saw in Mount Hebron (Num. 13:22) when they went in to explore the land.

people.name: Talmai
people.summary: One of the Anakim of Hebron, who were slain by the men of Judah under Caleb (Num. 13:22; Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

people.name: Achsah
people.summary: Anklet, Caleb’s only daughter (1 Chr. 2:49). She was offered in marriage to the man who would lead an attack on the city of Debir, or Kirjath-sepher.

people.name: Othniel
people.summary: Lion of God, the first of the judges. His wife Achsah was the daughter of Caleb (Josh. 15:16, 17; Judg. 1:13). He gained her hand as a reward for his bravery in leading a successful expedition against Debir.

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: Caleb’s younger brother, and father of Othniel (Josh. 15:17), whose family was of importance in Israel down to the time of David (1 Chr. 27:15).

places.name: Edom
places.summary: Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). “The field of Edom” (Gen. 32:3), “the land of Edom” (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).

places.name: Judah
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-0611 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Zin
places.summary: A low palm-tree, the south-eastern corner of the desert et-Tih, the wilderness of Paran, between the Gulf of Akabah and the head of the Wady Guraiyeh (Num. 13:21).

places.name: salt sea
places.summary: The name given by Greek writers of the second century to that inland sea called in Scripture the “salt sea” (Gen. 14:3; Num. 34:12), the “sea of the plain” (Deut. 3:17), the “east sea” (Ezek. 47:18; Joel 2:20), and simply “the sea” (Ezek. 47:8).

places.name: Adar
places.summary: Large, the sixth month of the civil and the twelfth of the ecclesiastical year of the Jews (Esther 3:7, 13; 8:12; 9:1, 15, 17, 19, 21). It included the days extending from the new moon of our March to the new moon of April.

places.name: Akrabbim
places.summary: Scorpions, probably the general name given to the ridge containing the pass between the south of the Dead Sea and Zin, es-Sufah, by which there is an ascent to the level of the land of Palestine.

places.name: Hezron
places.summary: A plain in the south of Judah, west of Kadesh-barnea (Josh. 15:3).

places.name: Kadesh-barnea
places.summary: Holy, or Kadesh-Barnea, sacred desert of wandering, a place on the south-eastern border of Palestine, about 165 miles from Horeb. It lay in the “wilderness” or “desert of Zin” (Gen. 14:7; Num. 13:3-26; 14:29-33; 20:1; 27:14), on the border of Edom (20:16).

places.name: Karka
places.summary: A floor; bottom, a place between Adar and Azmon, about midway between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea (Josh. 15:3).

places.name: Zin
places.summary: A low palm-tree, the south-eastern corner of the desert et-Tih, the wilderness of Paran, between the Gulf of Akabah and the head of the Wady Guraiyeh (Num. 13:21).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Beth-arabah
places.summary: House of the desert, one of the six cities of Judah, situated in the sunk valley of the Jordan and Dead Sea (Josh. 18:22). In Josh. 15:61 it is said to have been “in the wilderness.”

places.name: Adummim
places.summary: The red ones, a place apparently on the road between Jericho and Jerusalem, “on the south side of the torrent” Wady Kelt, looking toward Gilgal, mentioned Josh. 15:7; 18:17.

places.name: Debir
places.summary: A place near the “valley of Achor” (Josh. 15:7), on the north boundary of Judah, between Jerusalem and Jericho.

places.name: En-rogel
places.summary: Fountain of the treaders; i.e., “foot-fountain;” also called the “fullers’ fountain,” because fullers here trod the clothes in water. It has been identified with the “fountain of the virgin”, the modern ‘Ain Ummel-Daraj.

places.name: En-shemesh
places.summary: Fountain of the sun a spring which formed one of the landmarks on the boundary between Judah and Benjamin (Josh. 15:7; 18:17). It was between the “ascent of Adummim” and the spring of En-rogel, and hence was on the east of Jerusalem and of the Mount of Olives.

places.name: Gilgal
places.summary: From the solemn transaction of the reading of the law in the valley of Shechem between Ebal and Gerizim the Israelites moved forward to Gilgal, and there made a permanent camp (Josh. 9:6; 10:6).

places.name: valley of Achor
places.summary: Trouble, a valley near Jericho, so called in consequence of the trouble which the sin of Achan caused Israel (Josh. 7:24, 26). The expression “valley of Achor” probably became proverbial for that which caused trouble, and when Isaiah (Isa. 65:10) refers to it he uses it in this sense: “The valley of Achor, a place for herds to lie down in;” i.e., that which had been a source of calamity would become a source of blessing.

places.name: Jebusite
places.summary: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: valley of Hinnom
places.summary: A deep, narrow ravine separating Mount Zion from the so-called “Hill of Evil Counsel.” It took its name from “some ancient hero, the son of Hinnom.”

places.name: valley of Rephaim
places.summary: (Josh. 15:8; 18:16, R.V.). When David became king over all Israel, the Philistines, judging that he would now become their uncompromising enemy, made a sudden attack upon Hebron, compelling David to retire from it.

places.name: Baalah
places.summary: A city on the northern border of the tribe of Judah (Josh. 15:10), called also Kirjath-jearim, (15:9; 1 Chr. 13:6), now Kuriet-el-Enab, or as some think, ‘Erma.

places.name: Kiriath-jearim
places.summary: City, a city belonging to Benjamin (Josh. 18:28), the modern Kuriet el-‘Enab, i.e., “city of grapes”, about 7 1/2 miles west-north-west of Jerusalem.

places.name: mount Ephron
places.summary: A mountain range which formed one of the landmarks on the north boundary of the tribe of Judah (Josh. 15:9), probably the range on the west side of the Wady Beit-Hanina.

places.name: Nephtoah
places.summary: Opened, a fountain and a stream issuing from it on the border between Judah and Benjamin (Josh. 15:8, 9; 18:15). It has been identified with ‘Ain Lifta, a spring about 2 1/2 miles north-west of Jerusalem.

places.name: Beth-shemesh
places.summary: A sacerdotal city in the tribe of Dan (Josh. 21:16; 1 Sam. 6:15), on the north border of Judah (Josh. 15:10). It was the scene of an encounter between Jehoash, king of Israel, and Amaziah, king of Judah, in which the latter was made prisoner (2 Kings 14:11, 13).

places.name: Chesalon
places.summary: Strength; confidence, a place on the border of Judah, on the side of Mount Jearim (Josh. 15:10); probably identified with the modern village of Kesla, on the western mountains of Judah.

places.name: mount Jearim
places.summary: Forests, a mountain on the border of Judah (Josh. 15:10).

places.name: mount Seir
places.summary: A mountain range (not the Edomite range, Gen. 32:3) lying between the Wady Aly and the Wady Ghurab (Josh. 15:10).

places.name: Timnah
places.summary: A town of Judah (Josh. 15:10). The Philistines took possession of it in the days of Ahaz (2 Chr. 28:18). It was about 20 miles west of Jerusalem.

places.name: Ekron
places.summary: Firm-rooted, the most northerly of the five towns belonging to the lords of the Philistines, about 11 miles north of Gath. It was assigned to Judah (Josh. 13:3), and afterwards to Dan (19:43), but came again into the full possession of the Philistines (1 Sam. 5:10).

places.name: Jabneel
places.summary: A town in the north boundary of Judah (Josh. 15:11), called afterwards by the Greeks Jamnia, the modern Yebna, 11 miles south of Jaffa.

places.name: mount Baalah
places.summary: A mountain on the north-western boundary of Judah and Dan (Josh. 15:11).

places.name: great sea
places.summary: (Joel 2:20; Ezek. 47:18), the Dead Sea, which lay on the east side of the Holy Land.

places.name: Hebron
places.summary: A city in the south end of the valley of Eshcol, about midway between Jerusalem and Beersheba, from which it is distant about 20 miles in a straight line.

places.name: Negeb
places.summary: Heb. Negeb, that arid district to the south of Palestine through which lay the caravan route from Central Palestine to Egypt (Gen. 12:9; 13:1, 3; 46:1-6).

places.name: Eder
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah, on the border of Idumea (Josh. 15:21).

places.name: Jagur
places.summary: Place of sojourn, a city on the southern border of Judah (Josh. 15:21).

places.name: Kabzeel
places.summary: Gathering of God, a city in the extreme south of Judah, near to Idumaea (Josh. 15:21), the birthplace of Benaiah, one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 23:20; 1 Chr. 11:22).

places.name: Kinah
places.summary: An elegy, a city in the extreme south of Judah (Josh. 15:22).

places.name: Hazor
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:23).

places.name: Bealoth
places.summary: Citizens, a town in the extreme south of Judah (Josh. 15:24); probably the same as Baalath-beer (19:8).

places.name: Telem
places.summary: A town in the southern border of Judah (Josh. 15:24); probably the same as Telaim.

places.name: Ziph
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:24), probably at the pass of Sufah.

places.name: Hazor-hadattah
places.summary: New Hazor, a city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:25).

places.name: Kerioth-hezron
places.summary: A town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:25). Judas the traitor was probably a native of this place, and hence his name Iscariot.

places.name: Moladah
places.summary: Birth, a city in the south of Judah which fell to Simeon (Josh. 15:21-26; 19:2).

places.name: Shema
places.summary: A town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:26); the same as Sheba (ver. 5).

places.name: Hazar-gaddah
places.summary: Village of fortune, a city on the south border of Judah (Josh. 15:27), midway between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea.

places.name: Heshmon
places.summary: Fatness, a town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:27).

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Gen. 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Gen. 26:31-33).

places.name: Hazar-shual
places.summary: Village or enclosure of the jackal, a city on the south border of Judah (Josh. 15:28; Neh. 11:27).

places.name: Baalah
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:29), elsewhere called Balah (Josh. 19:3) and Bilhah (1 Chr. 4:29).

places.name: Iim
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:29).

places.name: Chesil
places.summary: Ungodly, a town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:30); probably the same as Bethul (19:4) and Bethuel (1 Chr. 4:30); now Khelasa.

places.name: Hormah
places.summary: Banning; i.e., placing under a “ban,” or devoting to utter destruction. After the manifestation of God’s anger against the Israelites, on account of their rebellion and their murmurings when the spies returned to the camp at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Paran, with an evil report of the land, they quickly repented of their conduct, and presumed to go up “to the head of the mountain,” seeking to enter the Promised Land, but without the presence of the Lord, without the ark of…

places.name: Madmannah
places.summary: Dunghill, the modern el-Minyay, 15 miles south-south-west of Gaza (Josh. 15:31; 1 Chr. 2:49), in the south of Judah. The Pal.

places.name: Sansannah
places.summary: A palm branch, or a thorn bush, a town in the south (the negeb) of Judah (Josh. 15:31); called also Hazarsusah (19:5), or Hazar-susim (1 Chr. 4:31).

places.name: Ziklag
places.summary: A town in the Negeb, or south country of Judah (Josh. 15:31), in the possession of the Philistines when David fled to Gath from Ziph with all his followers.

places.name: Rimmon
places.summary: One of the “uttermost cities” of Judah, afterwards given to Simeon (Josh. 15:21, 32; 19:7; 1 Chr. 4:32). In Josh. 15:32 Ain and Rimmon are mentioned separately, but in 19:7 and 1 Chr. 4:32 (comp. Neh. 11:29) the two words are probably to be combined, as forming together the name of one place, Ain-Rimmon=the spring of the pomegranate.

places.name: Shilhim
places.summary: Aqueducts, a town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:32); called also Sharuhen and Shaaraim (19:6).

places.name: Eshtaol
places.summary: Narrow pass or recess, a town (Josh. 15:33) in the low country, the She-phelah of Judah. It was allotted to the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:41), and was one of their strongholds.

places.name: Zorah
places.summary: Place of wasps, a town in the low country of Judah, afterwards given to Dan (Josh. 19:41; Judg. 18:2), probably the same as Zoreah (Josh. 15:33).

places.name: En-gannim
places.summary: A town in the plains of Judah (Josh. 15:34), north-west of Jerusalem, between Zanoah and Tappuah.

places.name: Tappuah
places.summary: A town in the valley or lowland of Judah; formerly a royal city of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:17; 15:34).

places.name: Zanoah
places.summary: A town in the low country or shephelah of Judah, near Zorah (Josh. 15:34). It was re-occupied after the return from the Captivity (Neh. 11:30).

places.name: Adullam
places.summary: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites, now ‘Aid-el-ma (Josh. 12:15; 15:35). It stood on the old Roman road in the valley of Elah, which was the scene of David’s memorable victory over Goliath (1 Sam. 17:2), and not far from Gath.

places.name: Azekah
places.summary: Dug over, a town in the Shephelah or low hills of Judah (Josh. 15:35), where the five confederated Amoritish kings were defeated by Joshua and their army destroyed by a hailstrom (10:10, 11).

places.name: Jarmuth
places.summary: A town in the plain of Judah (Josh. 15:35), originally the residence of one of the Canaanitish kings (10:3, 5, 23).

places.name: Gederah
places.summary: The fortress; a fortified place, a town in the plain (shephelah) of Judah (Josh. 15:36). This is a very common Canaanite and Phoenician name.

places.name: Shaaraim
places.summary: A city in the plain of Judah (1 Sam. 17:52); called also Sharaim (Josh. 15:36).

places.name: Hadashah
places.summary: New, a city in the valley of Judah (Josh. 15:37).

places.name: Migdal-gad
places.summary: Tower of fortune, a town in the plains of Judah, probably the modern el-Mejdel, a little to the north-east of Ascalon (Josh. 15:37).

places.name: Eglon
places.summary: A city in Judah, near Lachish (Josh. 15:39). It was destroyed by Joshua (10:5, 6).

places.name: Lachish
places.summary: Impregnable, a royal Canaanitish city in the Shephelah, or maritime plain of Palestine (Josh. 10:3, 5; 12:11). It was taken and destroyed by the Israelites (Josh. 10:31-33).

places.name: Chitlish
places.summary: A man’s wall, a town in the plain of Judah (Josh. 15:40).

places.name: Beth-dagon
places.summary: A city in the low country or plain of Judah, near Philistia (Josh. 15:41); the modern Beit Degan, about 5 miles from Lydda.

places.name: Makkedah
places.summary: Herdsman’s place, one of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:16), near which was a cave where the five kings who had confederated against Israel sought refuge (10:10-29).

places.name: Naamah
places.summary: A city in the plain of Judah (Josh. 15:41), supposed by some to be identified with Na’aneh, some 5 miles south-east of Makkedah.

places.name: Libnah
places.summary: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites taken by Joshua (Josh. 10:29-32; 12:15). It became one of the Levitical towns in the tribe of Judah (21:13), and was strongly fortified.

places.name: Nezib
places.summary: A town in the “plain” of Judah.

places.name: Achzib
places.summary: A town in the Shephelah, or plain country of Judah (Josh. 15:44); probably the same as Chezib of Gen. 38:5 = Ain Kezbeh.

places.name: Keilah
places.summary: Citadel, a city in the lowlands of Judah (Josh. 15:44). David rescued it from the attack of the Philistines (1 Sam. 23:1-8); but the inhabitants proving unfaithful to him, in that they sought to deliver him up to Saul (13), he and his men “departed from Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go.”

places.name: Mareshah
places.summary: Possession, a city in the plain of Judah (John. 15:44). Here Asa defeated Zerah the Ethiopian (2 Chr. 14:9, 10).

places.name: Ashdod
places.summary: Stronghold, a Philistine city (Josh. 15:47), about midway between Gaza and Joppa, and 3 miles from the Mediterranean. It was one of the chief seats of the worship of Dagon (1 Sam. 5:5).

places.name: Gaza
places.summary: Called also Azzah, which is its Hebrew name (Deut. 2:23; 1 Kings 4:24; Jer. 25:20), strong, a city on the Mediterranean shore, remarkable for its early importance as the chief centre of a great commercial traffic with Egypt.

places.name: Jattir
places.summary: Pre-eminent, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:48; 21:14).

places.name: Shamir
places.summary: A town among the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:48); probably Somerah, 2 1/2 miles north-west of Debir.

places.name: Dannah
places.summary: Murmuring, a city (Josh. 15:49) in the mountains of Judah about 8 miles south-west of Hebron.

places.name: Anab
places.summary: Grape-town, one of the cities in the mountains of Judah, from which Joshua expelled the Anakim (Josh. 11:21; 15:50). It still retains its ancient name.

places.name: Anim
places.summary: Fountains, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:50), now el-Ghuwein, near Eshtemoh, about 10 miles south-west of Hebron.

places.name: Giloh
places.summary: Exile, a city in the south-west part of the hill-country of Judah (Josh. 15:51). It was the native place or residence of the traitor Ahithophel “the Gilonite” (Josh. 15:51; 2 Sam. 15:12), and where he committed suicide (17:23).

places.name: Goshen
places.summary: A district in Palestine (Josh. 10:41; 11:16).

places.name: Arab
places.summary: Ambush, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:52), now Er-Rabiyeh.

places.name: Eshan
places.summary: A place in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:52), supposed to be the ruin es-Simia, near Dumah, south of Hebron.

places.name: Beth-tappuah
places.summary: House of apples, a town of Judah, now Tuffuh, 5 miles west of Hebron (Josh. 15:53).

places.name: Janim
places.summary: Slumber, a town in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:53).

places.name: Zior
places.summary: Littleness, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:54); the modern Si’air, 4 1/2 miles north-north-east of Hebron.

places.name: Carmel
places.summary: A town in the hill country of Judah (Josh. 15:55), the residence of Nabal (1 Sam. 25:2, 5, 7, 40), and the native place of Abigail, who became David’s wife (1 Sam. 27:3).

places.name: Juttah
places.summary: Extended, a Levitical city in the mountains or hill-country of Judah (Josh. 15:55; 21:16). Its modern name is Yutta, a place about 5 1/2 miles south of Hebron.

places.name: Maon
places.summary: Habitation, a town in the tribe of Judah, about 7 miles south of Hebron, which gave its name to the wilderness, the district round the conical hill on which the town stood.

places.name: Ziph
places.summary: A city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:55), identified with the uninhabited ruins of Tell ez-Zif, about 5 miles south-east of Hebron.

places.name: Jezreel
places.summary: A town in Judah (Josh. 15:56), to the south-east of Hebron.

places.name: Jokdeam
places.summary: A city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:56).

places.name: Zanoah
places.summary: A town in the hill country of Judah, some 10 miles to the south-west of Hebron (Josh. 15:56).

places.name: Gibeah
places.summary: (Josh. 15:57, R.V. marg.), a city on Mount Ephraim which had been given to Phinehas (24:33 “hill,” A.V.; R.V. marg. and Heb., “Gibeah.”). Here Eleazar the son of Aaron was buried.

places.name: Kain
places.summary: A town of the Kenites, a branch of the Midianites (Josh. 15:57), on the east edge of the mountain above Engedi; probably the “nest in a rock” mentioned by Balaam (Num. 24:21).

places.name: Timnah
places.summary: A city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:57)= Tibna near Jeba’.

places.name: Gedor
places.summary: A town apparently in Benjamin (1 Chr. 12:7), the same probably as Geder (Josh. 12:13).

places.name: Halhul
places.summary: Full of hollows, a town in the highlands of Judah (Josh. 15:58). It is now a small village of the same name, and is situated about 5 miles north-east of Hebron on the way to Jerusalem.

places.name: Beth-anoth
places.summary: House of answers, a city in the mountainous district of Judah (Josh. 15:59).

places.name: Eltekon
places.summary: from tyndale

places.name: Maarath
places.summary: Desolation, a place in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:59), probably the modern village Beit Ummar, 6 miles north of Hebron.

places.name: Rabbah
places.summary: “Rabbath of the children of Ammon,” the chief city of the Ammonites, among the eastern hills, some 20 miles east of the Jordan, on the southern of the two streams which united with the Jabbok.

places.name: Middin
places.summary: Measures, one of the six cities “in the wilderness,” on the west of the Dead Sea, mentioned along with En-gedi (Josh. 15:61).

places.name: Secacah
places.summary: Enclosure, one of the six cities in the wilderness of Judah, noted for its “great cistern” (Josh. 15:61).

places.name: Engedi
places.summary: Fountain of the kid, place in the wilderness of Judah (Josh. 15:62), on the western shore of the Dead Sea (Ezek. 47:10), and nearly equidistant from both extremities.

places.name: Nibshan
places.summary: Fertile; light soil, a city somewhere “in the wilderness” of Judah (Josh. 15:62), probably near Engedi.

places.name: Salt
places.summary: One of the cities of Judah (Josh. 15:62), probably in the Valley of Salt, at the southern end of the Dead Sea.
